title: Roles: assuming one, the trust policy and cross-account access

videos.script: A role is a door with a lock on each side. This lesson opens one, and then tries to open it without the key. {{both}} To assume a role, two policies have to agree. Your own policy must allow you to ask. And the role's trust policy must name you. {{caio}} In the lab, an administrator with every permission is turned away, because the trust policy names someone else. {{session}} What comes back is a session. It has the role's permissions, not yours, and it ends on its own. Fifteen minutes at least, an hour by default, twelve at most. {{chain}} Sessions can chain, one role into another, and the log has to say who started it. {{accounts}} Then the door opens between accounts. From the management account into production. And from a monitoring company, which brings a code called an external id. Without it, another customer could borrow the company's access to reach yours. {{end}}
